full_judgment:
Sikder Maqbul Huq J : The instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceedings of Sessions Case No. 211 of 2007 arising out of Belkuchi Police Station Case No. 01 dated 8-7-2007 corresponding to GR Case No. 66 of 2007 under sections 19(1) table 7(b) of the Madak Drabya Niantron Ain, 1990 (hereinafter referred to as the Ain) now pending in the Court of Sessions Judge, Serajganj, should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Prosecution case, in a nutshell, is that Iqbal Anwar, Sub-Inspector of Belkuchi Police Station, on the basis of a secret information on 8-7-2007 at 9-00 PM, recovered 5(five) bundles of cannabis, weighing about 3(three) maunds, worth Taka 6,00,000 (six lac) only from the house of accused-petitioner Md Liton Bhuiyan @ Md Liton Mia seized the same on the basis of a seizure list in presence of witnesses, arrested the accused-petitioner and lodged the FIR on the same date at 23-30 hours. Another Sub-Inspector of the said Police Station namely, MA Momin, being entrusted with investigation by the Officer-in-Charge, investigated into the case and submitted charge sheet against the accused- petitioner and another, being his brother-in-law. 

 4. After submission of the charge sheet, the concerned Magistrate sent the case to the learned Sessions Judge who took cognizance of an offence under sections 19(1) table 7(b) of the said Ain. 

 5. The learned Sessions Judge framed charge against the accused persons under the. aforesaid section of the Ain and examined 4 witnesses where- after accused-petitioner Md Liton Bhuiyan @ Md Liton Mia has preferred the instant application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceedings of the Sessions Case. 

 6. Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, submits that the Informant being a Sub- Inspector of Police had no authority to make any search, seizure or to arrest the accused-petitioner in connection with an offence under the said Ain as per provisions of sections 36 and 41 thereof and, as such, the continuation of the proceedings is nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court. Mr Rahman further submits that no Officer other than the Officer-in-Charge of Police Station has any legal authority to hold any investigation of the alleged offence as per provision of section 39 of the said Ain and the sessions case, having been started upon a report submitted by an unlawful authority, must be quashed. 

 7. Mr Rahman lastly submits that no Police Officer without the permission of the Director General of Madak Drabya Niantron Adidaptor has any authority to investigate into a case under the said Ain and on this ground also the proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 8. Mr Md Iqbal Kabir, learned Assistant Attorney-General, appearing for the State, on the other hand, submits that the application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is wholly misconceived and the inherent power of Police to investigate into a criminal case, has in no way, been taken away by the provisions of the said Ain. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further submits that as about 3(three) maunds of cannabis has been recovered from him in presence of the witnesses on the basis of a seizure list by the Informant and the members of the force accompanying him, the accused-petitioner, with a view to delay the proceeding and, also, in order to avoid legal punishment, has filed this petition at a too belated stage with ulterior motive and, as such, the Rule should be discharged. 

 10. Thus, it is apparent from a plain reading of this sections as amended in 2000 AD (Act 39 of 2000) that a Sub-Inspector of Police or any Police Officer of the higher rank, if he has any reason to believer that an offence under this Ain has been or is being committed or is likely to be committed in any place, he may, after recording the reason for such belief, at any time, enter into the premises and search and also seize any Madak Drabya or articles used in commission of the offence and also take further steps that may be necessary. This section only has given the Director General or any Officer authorised generally or specially in this behalf by him the power to search, seize, etc. Thus, this section does not take away the power of a Police Officer to make search, seizure, initiate a proceeding or to investigate into a case under the provisions of the said Ain. 

 12. There is nothing in section 39 of this Ain taking away the power of a Police Officer to make any search or seizure or initiate or investigate a case under the provisions of this Ain. This section only confers powers, for the purposes of this Ain, of an Officer-in-Charge of a Police Station, upon the Director General of Madak Drabya Niantron Adhidaptor and the government may also confer such power by Gazette Notification to any other Officer subordinate to the said Director General. Let us now quote section 41 of the said Ain. 

 13. This section, also, does not put any embargo on the power of a Police Officer to make search, seizure or to arrest any person or to investigate into a case and there is also nothing in the said Ain requiring a Police Officer to obtain prior permission of the Director General of Madak Drabya Niantron Adhidaptor to investigate into a case or to search, seize and to arrest any person who has committed or is committing or is likely to commit an offence under the said Ain. 

 15. In view of the aforesaid discussion it is apparent that the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is wholly misconceived and the application has been made with an ulterior motive to delay the proceeding of the case. 

 16. The upshot of the above discussion is that a Sub-Inspector of Police or an Officer above has inherent power to investigate into an offence in accordance with law and he has also been specially empowered by section 36(1) of The Madak Drabya Niantron Ain to search, seize, arrest, to initiate a case and to investigate into a case under this Ain and he needs no permission of the Director General of Madak Drabya Niantron Adhidaptor for investigating into a case under the provisions of this Ain. He is, however, required to make a report of the arrest, etc to his superior officer under section 38 of the said Ain and to send a copy thereof to the Director General.
